identification.summary: CrowdStrike describes TRACER KITTEN as an Iran-based adversary active since at least 2016 with a suspected link to the Iranian government [S2]. In April 2020 CrowdStrike Falcon OverWatch observed it conducting interactive activity against multiple hosts at a telecommunications company in the EMEA region, operating under valid user accounts with custom backdoors and SSH tunnels for C2 [S3].
identification.notes: CrowdStrike name; no Microsoft name or other vendor aliases were found in the sources gathered. Do not confuse with other CrowdStrike Kitten adversaries (e.g. PIONEER KITTEN, ARCANE KITTEN) or with Mirage Kitten/Tortoiseshell, which are separate clusters.

attribution.sponsor: CrowdStrike states a suspected link to the Iranian government [S2].
attribution.confidence: CrowdStrike labels the government link 'suspected' [S2]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: CrowdStrike Falcon OverWatch threat hunting and adversary profile [S2]; specific indicators underlying the assessment are not public in the sources gathered.

objectives: CrowdStrike assesses the group likely serves Iranian intelligence needs regarding telecommunications entities [S2]. In the 2020 intrusion it performed reconnaissance, credential harvesting and prepared for data exfiltration [S3].

targeting.notes: Targeting per CrowdStrike profile snippet and the 2020 OverWatch case [S2].

capabilities.summary: In the April 2020 case the actor used valid user accounts, custom backdoors and SSH tunnels for C2, with reconnaissance, credential harvesting and exfiltration preparation [S3]. CrowdStrike's profile indicates activity begins with compromise of victim web servers; the rest of that description was not retrievable [S2]. A secondary listing notes no exploited CVEs have been tied to the group [S4].

campaigns.name: Earliest CrowdStrike-reported activity
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike states the adversary has been active since at least 2016 [S2].

campaigns.name: EMEA telecommunications intrusion
campaigns.summary: Falcon OverWatch discovered interactive activity on multiple hosts at an EMEA telecom, using valid accounts, custom backdoors and SSH tunnel C2, with recon, credential harvesting and exfiltration preparation [S3].

diamond.adversary: Iran-based, suspected Iranian government link per CrowdStrike [S2].
diamond.capability: Custom backdoors, valid accounts, SSH tunnels, credential harvesting [S3]; web-server compromise [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: SSH tunnels used for C2 [S3]; compromised victim web servers [S2].
diamond.victim: Telecommunications entities in the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia; an EMEA telecom in 2020 [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Likely serves Iranian intelligence requirements on telecommunications [S2].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing web servers and telecom enterprise hosts with valid-credential access [S2].

gaps: The CrowdStrike adversary profile and Malpedia page could not be opened (fetch failed); the profile was read only through search-result snippets, which were truncated, and is undated.
The primary CrowdStrike OverWatch report 'Nowhere to Hide' (2020, dated 2020-09-15 per Malpedia) was not opened; the TRACER KITTEN text was seen via aggregator copies [S3][S4].
Custom backdoor names, infrastructure, and victim identities are unknown.
No activity after 2020 found; current status unknown.
Unclear whether the 2020 telecom case and the web-server compromise pattern in the profile are the same activity.
Basis for the 'suspected' Iranian government link is not public.
